title: Macaroni Cheese
subtitle: Baked pasta in a rich Cheddar and mustard sauce
excerpt: Macaroni pasta in a thick, sharp Cheddar sauce with English mustard and a bubbling, golden breadcrumb crust. The ultimate weeknight comfort dish.

recipe.sourceNotes: Macaroni cheese has been popular in Britain and America since the eighteenth century. Thomas Jefferson famously served it at a White House dinner in 1802, having encountered it in France. In Britain it appears in Mrs Beeton's Book of Household Management (1861) and has been a staple of school dinners and home cooking ever since. The sauce is a simple béchamel enriched with grated cheese: the sharper and more aged the cheese, the more flavour. English mustard is the traditional British addition, providing heat that cuts through the richness of the sauce. The breadcrumb topping is optional but adds texture. Cooking the macaroni slightly under-done before baking is important: it will absorb liquid from the sauce during the baking period and would become overcooked if fully cooked in advance.

recipeTools.notes: For the pasta and the sauce.

content.text: Cook the macaroni for 2 minutes less than the packet instructions. It finishes in the oven, so it needs to still be very slightly firm going in. Use a good aged Cheddar: mild cheese makes a flat, one-dimensional sauce. Add the cheese off the heat to prevent it becoming stringy. Make the sauce thicker than feels right, because the pasta will absorb liquid during baking.
Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Cook the macaroni in well-salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet instructions. Drain and set aside.

Melt the butter in the same saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the milk, adding it slowly at first. Simmer for 6 minutes, stirring regularly, until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Remove from the heat. Stir in 200 g of the Cheddar, the mustard, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Add the drained pasta and stir to coat. Transfer to a large oven-proof dish.
Mix together the breadcrumbs, remaining Cheddar, and Parmesan. Scatter over the top. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
